source.label: The Gram form's prime side as a weighted square integral

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: For L > 0, grid tau_k = tau_0 + 2 pi k/L, phi real even bounded with support in [-L/2, L/2], real finitely supported c and H_c = sum c_k phihat(. - tau_k): int H_c^2 = 2 pi int phi^2 |sum c_k e^{iu tau_k}|^2 <= 2 pi L ||phi||_inf^2 |c|^2, and for bounded real nu the form Q_nu(c) = sum c_k c_l int phihat(tau - tau_k) phihat(tau - tau_l) nu(tau) dtau equals int H_c^2 nu, so inf nu int H_c^2 <= Q_nu <= sup nu int H_c^2. For nu = cos(tau v) the diagonal entry is 2 pi (phi*phi)(v) cos(tau_k v), so for the truncated prime sum P_X of the density import, G^P_kk = -2 sum Lambda(n) n^{-1/2} (phi*phi)(log n) cos(tau_k log n).
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof (Plancherel, orthogonality over one period, Fourier inversion). As a bound for the prime part of the imported Gram form it is the trivial one, since sup|P_X| over the line is attained at 0; it returns delta <= 1/2 for a solitary pair in the model. The diagonal identity gives one proved implication, from an eigenvalue bound to a bound for smoothed prime sums at the grid heights. A bound by the size of P_X near [T, 2T] only needs a localization that is not proved; the smooth part with mu is not treated.
claims.rationale: Reads the prime side of the Gram form from the source's definitions and shows what an elementary bound gives (nothing beyond trivial) and which implication is proved; the sign lead stays open on a localization and a converse.
claims.next_action: Prove the localization of int H_c^2 near [T, 2T] for coefficients on the cut grid, then decide the positive-kernel one-sided form.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.
